Fill the head row of a script block from a result method

Source: R/result-head.R
result_head.Rd

A script block has one head row: the sentence on the left, the gear on the right. A block_result_output() method calls result_head() to put its own tools into that row, left of the gear, and to give the sentence titles for the lines the script does not declare.

Usage

result_head(session, tools = NULL, titles = NULL, caption = TRUE)

Arguments

session

The block's session, as the method received it.

tools

Tags for the head row, or NULL for none.

titles

A list with any of title, subtitle and caption, each one plain string. The sentence shows them for the lines the script does not declare. A line the script declares wins, and a script line with nothing after the colon (#| title:) switches that line off. The strings are shown as they are; {...} is not read in them.

caption

FALSE when the result draws the caption itself.

Value

NULL, invisibly.

Details

The head row starts empty before every render. A method that does not call result_head() leaves the row as the script block draws it, so the tools of one result class are gone as soon as the script returns another. The method is called on every re-evaluation; calling result_head() again with the same arguments redraws nothing. The tools are hidden while the block has no result on screen, for example after an error.

Tools

tools is drawn as it is. A direct child that is a link or a button gets the size and look of an icon button (26 px square), so give it an icon as its content and a title as its name. Ids are namespaced with session$ns() and their outputs and inputs live on session, as anywhere in the method. Assigning a downloadHandler to session$output on every call is fine. An observer on session$input must be created once per block and not once per call, see block_result_output().

Caption

The script block draws a #| caption: line in the head row, under the subtitle. A result that draws the caption itself, such as a table with the caption under it, passes caption = FALSE and reads the text from result_titles(). The head row then leaves the caption out, so there is one copy on screen. A control that only the caption names stays in the grid of controls, because the head row has no word for it.

See also

result_titles() for the sentence as text, block_result_output() for the method this is called from.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
block_result_output.my_table <- function(result, block, session, ...) {
  session$output$csv <- shiny::downloadHandler(
    filename = "table.csv",
    content = function(file) utils::write.csv(result$data, file)
  )
  result_head(
    session,
    tools = shiny::downloadLink(
      session$ns("csv"), label = shiny::icon("download"),
      title = "Download"
    ),
    titles = list(title = "My table"),
    caption = FALSE
  )
  shiny::renderUI(
    shiny::tagList(
      draw_my_table(result),
      shiny::tags$p(result_titles(session)$caption)
    )
  )
}
} # }
